scope: All 14 conceptual questions independently derived from original PDF27–28 diagrams and cross-compared with the final authored fields. All pass after corrections to Q10(c) and Q11(a).

questions.verification: A top-to-bottom path difference of 5λ closes five full phasor cycles, giving a minimum. At 4.5λ the point is near the fourth side maximum; the exact secondary maximum obeys tanα=α.
questions.comparison: Pass: all requested conclusions match the independently derived source interpretation.

questions.verification: A 4λ path difference gives total phase 8π, tracing four overlapping circles.
questions.comparison: Pass: all requested conclusions match the independently derived source interpretation.

questions.verification: β=πd sinθ/λ; the higher curve indicates larger slit separation and a greater number of allowed interference orders.
questions.comparison: Pass: all requested conclusions match the independently derived source interpretation.

questions.verification: α=πa sinθ/λ; the higher curve indicates a larger slit width and more allowed minima.
questions.comparison: Pass: all requested conclusions match the independently derived source interpretation.

questions.verification: Diffraction spreading varies inversely with the aperture dimension along the same transverse direction.
questions.comparison: Pass: all requested conclusions match the independently derived source interpretation.

questions.verification: Higher frequency shortens the vacuum wavelength; submersion shortens the internal wavelength. Both contract the pattern.
questions.comparison: Pass: all requested conclusions match the independently derived source interpretation.

questions.verification: Diffraction angles increase with wavelength, so red gives larger rings and lies at the outer edge.

questions.verification: Increasing d reduces diffraction angles, linewidth and dispersion. In Fig36-33 red lies left of green, so the longer red wavelength is farther left from the center; therefore the center is to the right and both lines shift right.

resolvedDiscrepancies.detail: Increasing grating spacing shifts the Fig36-33 lines RIGHT, toward the center indicated by the red-left/green-right ordering.
Grating A has thinner spectral lines and therefore more rulings than B.
